challenger.name: Fire and life-safety inspection company (code-mandated recurring ITM routes: sprinklers, alarms, extinguishers, backflow)
challenger.thesis: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157 and NFPA standards require every commercial building to have extinguishers, sprinklers, and alarms inspected on fixed schedules, which is why the fire-protection testing, inspection, and certification market was $1B in 2025 and heads to $1.27B by 2030 with maintenance services the largest recurring segment (https://www.researchandmarkets.com/report/fire-protection-system-testing-inspection-and-certification); a route-based inspection company sells 12-month contracts that renew forever, and every deficiency found converts into repair revenue.
challenger.why_now: The market is growing 4.6%-5.4% a year on regulatory and insurance mandates (ResearchAndMarkets above; https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/fire-protection-system-market-104820), and insurers are tightening commercial requirements after three straight years of $50B+ storm losses (https://www.iii.org/press-release/triple-i-severe-convective-storms-generate-more-than-50b-in-insured-losses-for-third-consecutive-year-041326). FIT: medium - needs a licensed technician; Joshua's edge is route-density selling, scheduling, and an inspection-reporting app.

dossier.key_numbers: backflow businesses $100-600K at ~35% margin; sprinkler ITM gross margin 50%+; shops valued 3-5x SDE with premiums for recurring ITM (https://bizbite.io/businesses/backflow-testing)
dossier.skeptic: Texas SFM licensing tiers (RME with NICET II for sprinkler inspection) mean starting with backflow and extinguishers and hiring licensed staff. Survives; consolidator exit (Pye-Barker) is the upside.

incumbent.name: Recurring-route pest control company built to 80%+ contract revenue (PE-exit spec)
incumbent.thesis: Launch for $15-65K all-in, break even in 6-14 months, and take home $80-140K by year two as a solo operator in a 200K+ metro (https://oncallclerk.com/blog/how-to-start-a-pest-control-business); 150 quarterly accounts at $80-120/visit is $480-720 per customer per year at 20-40% net margins (same source); then stack routes to $1M+ EBITDA, where 85%-recurring, sub-1.5%-monthly-churn books command 6.5-8x EBITDA and the recurring mix alone is worth a $2M valuation swing on a $1M-EBITDA business (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/pest-control-business-valuation/).
incumbent.why_now: $29.7B US market with 34,000+ operators and PE at ~60% of all pest M&A, with Anticimex, Arrow and Massey still aggressively acquisitive (https://www.breakwaterma.com/blog/pest-control-company-valuation-multiples-2026); pest control carries a 3.3x low / 5-6x mid / 8x+ high EBITDA band, top of the home-services stack (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/). Fit: route density is a lead-gen and dialer problem — Joshua's day job — and his RV-resort employer is a ready-made commercial anchor account.

dossier.key_numbers: solo take-home $80-140K by year 2, gross $135-300K, 25-50% margin once routed (https://www.fieldroutes.com/blog/how-profitable-is-pest-control-business; oncallclerk.com)
dossier.skeptic: Route density and a TDA applicator license are the gates; metros are crowded but Ark-La-Tex is not. Numbers hold. Survives.

challenger.name: Per-diem CNA/LVN/RN staffing pool for Ark-La-Tex hospitals, nursing homes and home-health agencies (run like a call center)
challenger.thesis: Healthcare staffing agencies bill a 40-60% markup over base wages (https://boostpoint.com/industries-healthcare/nurse-staffing-agency-costs/), paying a worker $25/hr and billing $38-45/hr yields a $13-20/hr spread or ~$31K gross margin per full-time-equivalent placement per year (https://naiori.ai/blog/staffing-agency-startup-costs-2026), startup cost is $3K-250K with 14-41% margins (https://naiori.ai/blog/staffing-agency-startup-costs-2026), and both Texarkana hospitals — now one CHRISTUS system — are openly fighting a nursing shortage with residencies and apprenticeships (https://www.christushealth.org/connect/news/expands-in-texarkana, https://www.themuse.com/jobs/christushealth/rn-registered-nurse-nurse-residency-octoberdecember-2025-f5b1e0) — 40 steady placements is $1.2M+ gross margin, and the core competency (recruit, dial, schedule, manage no-shows) is what Joshua already runs every day.
challenger.why_now: The CMS moratorium means existing home health/hospice agencies must grow rather than be replaced (https://hospicenews.com/2026/06/12/cms-moratorium-could-spur-hospice-home-health-ma/), rural Arkansas faces imminent retirement of aging clinicians (https://healthy.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/Office_of_Rural_Health_and_Primary_Care_Primary_Care_Needs_Assessment.pdf), and CNA recruiting campaigns now cost a median $7.72 per applicant with an 18% apply rate (https://boostpoint.com/industries-healthcare/cna-staffing/) — cheap acquisition for someone who already runs paid lead-gen.

dossier.key_numbers: 40-60% markup over base wage (boostpoint.com)
dossier.skeptic: Payroll float: you pay nurses weekly, facilities pay in 45-60 days (needs factoring); vendor-management systems gate hospitals; rates fell 2023-25. Survives.

incumbent.name: Fractional Head of Contact Center / RevOps for PE-Backed Multi-Location Healthcare (DSOs, med spas, PT, vet)
incumbent.thesis: PE-backed multi-location practices are centralizing scheduling and phones but cannot justify a $200K contact-center director per platform, so a fractional operator at $8K-15K/mo per platform running 3-5 platforms earns $300K-600K/yr plus equity kickers while designing the blended AI-plus-human phone stack they all need.
incumbent.why_now: Fractional VP-level RevOps already clears $10K-15K/mo in 2026, healthcare roll-ups face reimbursement pressure and must convert every inbound call, and AI phone agents are being sold into these platforms with no operator on the client side to make them work.

dossier.key_numbers: $8-15K/mo fractional retainers for PE-backed DSOs, med spas, PT, vet (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Relationship-sold; without a PE network the ramp is slow; competes with bigger-name ex-executives. Survives; among the highest reachable incomes for his exact resume.

pairing_reason: both healthcare-adjacent, staffing vs fractional exec

challenger.name: Non-medical home-care agency with a caregiver-recruiting dialer engine and a Medicaid CDS/FMSA arm
challenger.thesis: The U.S. home care market grew from $77B in 2020 to an estimated $113B in 2026 while BLS projects 17% employment growth and ~765,800 openings a year for home health and personal care aides through 2034 (https://www.aveecare.com/resources/home-care-industry-statistics-2026; https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/home-health-and-personal-care-aides.htm), a Texas non-medical agency launches for $7,000-15,000 plus a $2,625 three-year HCSSA license (https://123consultingsolutions.com/how-much-does-it-cost-to-start-a-home-care-business-in-texas; https://thebizofseniorcare.com/resources/how-to-start-a-home-care-agency-in-texas/), and Texas Medicaid pays family caregivers up to $2,205/month through STAR+PLUS/CDS (https://www.newporthomehealth.com/how-much-does-medicaid-pay-family-caregivers-texas/): the agency that also becomes an HHSC-contracted Financial Management Services Agency captures the payroll-administration fee on every family caregiver it enrolls.
challenger.why_now: Caregiver turnover runs 75-77% a year (aveecare), which is precisely why a recruiting-and-retention operator (Joshua manages rep hiring and attrition daily) beats mom-and-pop agencies; 90% of older adults say they want to age at home (https://www.premierhcinc.com/blog/home-care-statistics/); gross margins run 30-40% with ~9.7% net for average operators (howmuchtostart), so operational discipline is the entire game. Capital: under $50K; ceiling is a multi-million-dollar agency, and the CDS/FMSA arm is a recurring admin-fee stream other lenses will miss.

dossier.key_numbers: owner average $102.8K, top independents $270K, median net margin 9.7% (https://clarifycapital.com/blog/home-care-agency-owner-income-2025)
dossier.skeptic: Thin margins, 77% caregiver turnover, Texas HCSSA licensing 4-6 months, thousands of Texas agencies. Survives; the recruiting-engine edge is real.

challenger.name: ADAS Calibration Center (insurance-paid sublet work for body and glass shops)
challenger.thesis: 28.3% of collision repairs now require ADAS calibration per Q4 2025 CCC data (https://pennypincher.com/articles/insurance/auto/adas-repair-costs-insurance-windshield-calibration) at $300-$600 per calibration (https://www.caliber.com/services/auto-glass/auto-glass-calibration/how-much-does-adas-calibration-cost), paid by insurers under comprehensive/collision coverage (https://blog.glass.net/glass-quotes/adas-calibration-insurance-coverage/); a standalone calibration bay doing 8 jobs/day at $400 grosses ~$800K/yr (estimate) in a North American market of $1.3B in 2025 growing to $2.5B by 2033 (https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/adas-calibration-services-market-115495). Capital: likely $75K-$150K for targets, scan tools, and a level bay (estimate; no sourced figure found), so above the $50K default.
challenger.why_now: Windshield replacements now routinely exceed $1,500 because of calibration (pennypincher link above), and small-town body/glass shops cannot justify the equipment, so they sublet. The global market is valued at $5.24B in 2025 rising to $12.85B by 2034 (Fortune Business Insights). FIT: medium - requires a technician and shop; Joshua's edge is B2B sales to every body/glass shop in the Ark-La-Tex plus ops dashboards.

dossier.key_numbers: shops average $21.5K/mo ADAS revenue, $350-500 per calibration, ~70% margin, equipment ~$55K (https://www.revvhq.com/blog/adas-calibration-profitable-service-collision-shops); 28.3% of repairs need calibration (CCC)
dossier.skeptic: Texarkana has perhaps 25-30 body/glass shops; needs technical skill; insurers push shops in-house; $18K/yr equipment refresh. Survives.

incumbent.name: Diesel generator load-bank testing and fuel polishing for data centers, hospitals and telecom sites
incumbent.thesis: NFPA 110 and Joint Commission rules require annual load-bank tests and clean fuel on every backup generator, each visit bills $1,500-6,000, and there are thousands of new generators being installed across Texas and the South with almost no independent local testers.
incumbent.why_now: ERCOT's large-load queue has exploded past 100 GW of data-center and industrial requests, every one of those sites is installing rows of diesel gensets that must be tested and have fuel polished on a schedule, and the OEM service networks are backlogged months. Capital: $40-70K for a trailer-mounted resistive load bank and a fuel-polishing rig.

dossier.key_numbers: NFPA 110 annual load-bank tests; $1,500-6,000 per visit (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Needs generator/electrical competence and facility-manager relationships; safety liability. Mandated recurring demand is real and growing with data centers. Survives.

pairing_reason: both equipment-based technical service businesses riding a trend

challenger.name: Aged-Lead Reactivation AI SDR billed per booked appointment
challenger.thesis: Every appointment-driven sales org sits on tens of thousands of paid-for, unconverted leads carried at $0, so an AI SMS/voice agent that re-engages them under compliant consent and books appointments, billed $25-$150 per show with zero upfront, converts sunk cost into found revenue and can bill six figures per client per year.
challenger.why_now: Paid cost-per-lead rose sharply through 2024-2026 while LLM conversational agents became good enough to hold a natural multi-turn text conversation and hand off to a calendar; new state consent laws like Texas SB 140 favor operators who build consent-aware pipelines; and pay-per-show pricing removes buyer risk, which is exactly the pitch a dialer operator already knows how to make.

dossier.key_numbers: tens of thousands of paid, unconverted leads per sales org (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Aged leads carry consent-expiry and TCPA exposure; carrier spam-labeling crushes contact rates; dozens of shops sell the same thing. Survives on fit.

incumbent.name: Outbound contact-rate and TCPA / mini-TCPA compliance managed service for lead-gen call centers (DID reputation, branded calling, litigator scrub, Texas SB 140 desk)
incumbent.thesis: Outbound call centers lose half their answers to 'Spam Likely' labels and cannot run number-reputation operations themselves, so a boutique that owns DID inventory strategy, carrier registrations, Rich Call Data / branded caller ID setup, remediation tickets, rotation and weekly reputation monitoring bills $3K-10K/mo per client plus per-DID fees and proves ROI with answer-rate lift.
incumbent.why_now: January 2026 alone saw 3.9B robocalls, 53% of enterprise leaders report improper spam labels cutting contact rates, and branded calls answer at 62% vs 20% unbranded; carriers now sell RCD and branded display, but SMB call centers have nobody to operate it.

dossier.key_numbers: contact centers lose half their answers to spam labels; DID reputation ops sold as a managed service (generator source; his own DID dashboard is the product)
dossier.skeptic: Numeracle and Caller ID Reputation sell tooling, not ops, so the boutique gap is real; clients must be found outside his employer; attribution of contact-rate lift. Survives; strongest fit in the pool.

pairing_reason: both sell outbound automation to sales orgs

challenger.name: Forestry-mulching, land-clearing and pasture-conversion crew (high-flow skid steer + mulcher)
challenger.thesis: A $130-160K financed skid-steer-and-mulcher package bills $175-275 per hour or $1,500-3,500 per acre with one operator, so 25 billable hours a week grosses $250-350K with fuel and cutter teeth as the only real cost of goods.
challenger.why_now: Raw-land sales in East Texas and SW Arkansas to DFW and out-of-state buyers surged after 2020 and remain elevated; those buyers want brush gone without burn permits or hauling, and mulching is the fastest, most photogenic way to do it. Real capital need: $130-160K financed (~$20-30K down).

dossier.key_numbers: $175-275/hr or $1,500-3,500/acre, $130-160K financed package (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Equipment breakdowns, weather, and pasture demand tied to record cattle prices. Survives.

incumbent.name: Roll-off dumpster rental fleet with online self-booking
incumbent.thesis: One used hook-lift truck (~$80-100K) and fifteen steel cans (~$5-6K each) throw off $450-650 per haul plus tonnage overage, so a single driver-owner can gross $250-400K a year at 50%+ margins in a secondary market the national haulers ignore for small jobs.
incumbent.why_now: The owner-operators who built these routes in the 1990s are aging out and selling, ArkLaTex hail/tornado/flood rebuild cycles keep demand spiky, steel tariffs have pushed new-can prices up (protecting incumbents who already own iron), and WM/Republic still won't do a 10-yard driveway can on 24 hours notice. Real capital need: ~$120-150K, financeable with $25-35K down.

dossier.key_numbers: one-truck owner earnings $120-250K, $350-450K revenue with a driver, ~$90K to start, 18-24 month payback (https://www.curbwaste.com/dumpster-rental-business-profitability; quipli.com)
dossier.skeptic: Tipping fees, truck downtime and WM/Republic pricing; still one of the best-documented cash businesses at this capital level. Survives.

challenger.name: Texas public-adjusting firm for hail, wind, freeze and water claims (10% statutory fee)
challenger.thesis: Texas caps public-adjuster fees at 10% of the settlement under Tex. Ins. Code 4102.104 (https://insuranceclaimrecoverysupport.com/public-adjuster-in-texas/), and U.S. severe convective storms produced $51B in insured losses in 2025 - the third straight year above $50B, more than any other natural-disaster category (https://www.iii.org/press-release/triple-i-severe-convective-storms-generate-more-than-50b-in-insured-losses-for-third-consecutive-year-041326). A TDI-licensed PA who signs 100 underpaid roof/commercial claims a year at a $40K average settlement uplift collects ~$400K (estimate: 100 x $40K x 10%; uplift assumed). Start as a licensed adjuster at an existing firm, then own the shop.
challenger.why_now: Texas leads the nation in raw hail exposure and insurers are under acute pressure (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/news/severe-convective-storms/); Gallagher Re puts total 2025 economic SCS damages above $68B (Triple-I release above). Rising deductibles and depreciation holdbacks mean more underpaid claims to reopen. FIT: high - claims are sold by phone/door after every storm, and a call center can run intake for a licensed PA.

dossier.key_numbers: Texas caps PA fees at 10%; salaried PAs average $67-70K (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Salaries/Public-Insurance-Adjuster-Salary--in-Texas)
dossier.skeptic: Claim cycles run 6-12 months before a fee lands; Texas solicitation restrictions; hail-year dependence; insurers' appraisal tactics. Survives, lumpy.

incumbent.name: Buy a retiring owner's trades shop (HVAC / plumbing / septic / pest) with SBA 7(a), modernize marketing + dispatch, exit to a PE platform
incumbent.thesis: Trades businesses sell at 2.5-3.2x seller's discretionary earnings with the median deal at $350K on $165K SDE (https://joinaccredited.com/blog/best-small-businesses-to-buy-2026), SBA 7(a) allows 10% down on deals up to $5M (https://joinaccredited.com/blog/best-small-businesses-to-buy-2026), so ~$50K controls a ~$500K rural business paying its owner $165K+ from day one, and small-town sellers face far fewer bidders than the metro firms where PE has bought ~800 HVAC/plumbing/electrical companies since 2022 (https://www.inc.com/victoria-salves/millennials-buying-up-hvac-and-plumbing-companies/91368971) — Joshua's lead-gen, dialer, and rep-management skills applied to a business that currently has no CRM, no follow-up, and no online presence can plausibly double SDE inside 24 months.
incumbent.why_now: Boomers still own ~12 million private companies with mostly no succession plan (https://www.clearlyacquired.com/blog/silver-tsunami-what-it-means-for-buyers), SBA-backed acquisition loans hit a record 6,915 loans / $8.17B in FY2025 (https://www.marketingcode.com/industry-shift-forbes-millennials-blue-collar-ai-proof-6915-sba-loans-jul-2026/), and 2026 is described as the Silver Tsunami's peak (https://sugarland.fcbb.com/news/sugar-land-businesses-for-sale-retiring-owners) — rural Texas/Arkansas trades owners in their late 60s are the least-contested inventory in the country.

dossier.key_numbers: median HVAC sale $800K, owner shops trade 2-3.5x SDE, $1M+ EBITDA shops clear 5-10x, Champions Group went at 18.5x (https://www.bizbuysell.com/learning-center/valuation-benchmarks/hvac/; dealprospectors.com)
dossier.skeptic: SBA needs 10-20% down ($80-160K) and a personal guarantee; search-to-close 6-18 months; PE exit requires reaching $1M+ EBITDA. The arbitrage is real and his exact edge (marketing, dispatch, phones). Survives as the highest-ceiling reachable play.

pairing_reason: both evergreen hybrids with lumpy payoffs

challenger.name: Septic (OSSF) + water-well installation company for the west Bowie County / Miller County subdivision sprawl
challenger.thesis: Texarkana's housing review says west-side subdivisions are being forced onto wells and septic because utility expansion hasn't kept pace (https://www.txkmag.com/news/community-culture/housing-texarkana/), and every one of those lots is a $10-20K aerobic septic ticket (https://dillonseptic.com/aerobic-septic-system-cost-in-texas/) plus a $6-30K well (https://drillerdb.com/resources/well-owner/texas-well-guide) plus a mandatory $300-500/yr aerobic maintenance contract that compounds into recurring revenue (https://www.texassepticguide.com/learn/septic-maintenance-cost-texas) — two crews doing three installs a week is a $1.5-3M/yr business (estimate: 150 installs x $10-20K), entered with a TEEX Installer I course that requires no prior experience (https://teex.org/class/www302/) and where even employee Installer II roles post at $75-100K (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Ossf/-in-Austin,TX).
challenger.why_now: Texarkana home values rose 2.8% in the year to June 2026 and the city is waiving permit fees and streamlining inspections to force more housing starts (https://www.zillow.com/home-values/20782/texarkana-tx/, https://www.txkmag.com/news/community-culture/housing-texarkana/), while Texas needs 530K+ additional trades workers in 2026 (https://www.metaintro.com/blog/skilled-trade-jobs-construction-electrical-plumbing-careers-2026) — the bottleneck is installers, not lots. Starting capital ~$50K works with a financed used mini-excavator/backhoe and trailer (estimate based on used-equipment pricing; no direct source).

dossier.key_numbers: west-side subdivisions forced onto wells and septic (txkmag.com)
dossier.skeptic: Excavator plus OSSF installer license and a driller partner; established local installers. Survives.

Real capital need: ~$120-150K, financeable with $25-35K down.

dossier.skeptic: Tipping fees, truck downtime and WM/Republic pricing; still one of the best-documented cash businesses at this capital level. Survives.

challenger.name: Texas storm-restoration roofing sales (1099 commission closer who also runs his own appointment pipeline)
challenger.thesis: Texas roofing sales self-reports at a $206,421 average with a $354K 90th percentile on Glassdoor (https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/texas-roofing-sales-salary-SRCH_IL.0,5_IS1347_KO6,19.htm) while ZipRecruiter puts storm-damage roofing sales at a more sober $73,891 average (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Storm-Damage-Roofing-Sales/--in-Texas); commissions run 8-15% of gross or 25-50% of profit (https://theroofingbrief.com/roofing-sales-jobs/) and first-year reps average ~$150K with top closers $250K+ (https://www.ghostrep.ai/blog/how-much-do-roofing-sales-reps-make) — the gap between those numbers is lead flow, which is the exact skill he already sells for a living.
challenger.why_now: Severe convective storms caused $52B+ in US insured losses in 2025, the third-highest on record, with Texas at the epicenter (https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2026/09/16/340002.htm, https://uphelp.org/texas-is-entering-peak-hail-season-and-most-homeowners-dont-understand-the-deductible-that-could-cost-them-thousands/?print=pdf); Texas still logged 319 severe hail events in H1 2026 even though reports were ~70% below the 2023-25 average (https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/insights/insurance/united-states-severe-convective-storm-losses-quieter-and-less-costly-during-first-half-2026.html) — so this is a structural-exposure bet, not a 2026-season bet; carriers' new ACV roof schedules and 1-3% wind/hail deductibles (https://www.latentinsure.com/blog/texas-hail-damage-home-insurance) reward reps who can supplement claims correctly.

dossier.key_numbers: $75K is the floor for a decent fit, $150K mid-range target; Glassdoor's $206K average is self-reported (https://blog.theroofstrategist.com/roofing-sales-income-how-much-you-really-should-make/)
dossier.skeptic: Texas insurers moving to ACV roof schedules and higher wind/hail deductibles shrink the supplement-driven model; hail-year dependent. Survives with the headline cut in half.

incumbent.name: Enterprise Account Executive selling AI voice/chat agents into contact centers
incumbent.thesis: Enterprise AE median OTE is $280K as of September 2026 (https://www.repvue.com/salaries/enterprise-account-executive) and AI-agent vendors such as Decagon are posting Enterprise AE roles at $230K-$320K (https://builtin.com/job/enterprise-account-executive/7280463); an operator who has personally run dialers, reps, lead gen and show-rate math is the rare seller who can credibly walk a VP of Contact Center through replacing seats, which is the fastest route from ops leadership to a $250K+ W-2.
incumbent.why_now: Forrester predicts 30% of enterprises will stand up parallel AI functions mirroring human service roles by end of 2026, and the conversational AI market is projected at $41.39B by 2030 at 23.7% CAGR (https://www.retellai.com/blog/will-ai-replace-call-center-agents); vendors explicitly want reps who have sold or deployed Sierra/Decagon/Parloa/Cognigy/Retell (https://builtin.com/job/account-executive/4453778); the highest-paying AE employers in 2026 include OpenAI at a $480K median OTE (https://www.repvue.com/salaries/enterprise-account-executive).

dossier.key_numbers: Enterprise AE median OTE $280K, top performers $677K, 12,819 submissions (https://www.repvue.com/salaries/enterprise-account-executive)
dossier.skeptic: Enterprise AE hires want a closing record; a first AI-vendor role is more likely mid-market ($120-160K OTE) with his contact-center domain as the hook. Survives at reduced probability.

challenger.name: Mobile RV repair technician (RVTI-certified) serving resorts and long-term residents
challenger.thesis: RV techs are so scarce that a mobile tech with a $15-25K van-and-tools kit bills $135-185 per hour plus parts markup and a $75-125 trip fee, clearing $120-180K solo before adding a second van.
challenger.why_now: The industry's own workforce data shows a multi-thousand-technician shortage with dealer service waits of weeks to months; RVTI Level 1-2 certification takes months online, not years; long-term RV living has grown with housing costs; and Joshua's resort network is a captive referral source.

dossier.key_numbers: $135-185/hr plus trip fee, RV techs scarce (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Needs RVTI certification and hands-on skill (6-12 months); physical work. Survives.

incumbent.name: Forward-deployed AI engineer / AI implementation contractor (voice and contact-center AI vendors)
incumbent.thesis: FDE job listings spiked ~800% with total comp of $200K-$630K+ (https://www.paraform.com/insights/forward-deployed-ai-engineer), a competent mid-level FDE earns $180-260K (https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-full-guide) and Palantir's FDSE median is $215K (https://getperspective.ai/blog/2026-forward-deployed-engineering-compensation-report-1200-fdes); someone who ships production apps with AI coding tools AND has lived inside a call center is exactly the deploy-into-the-customer profile, and the same skills sell as 12-24 month implementation contracts at $60-86/hr (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Ai-Implementation-Specialist).
incumbent.why_now: Voice AI specialists earn $39-60/hr median with 25-40% premiums for LLM fine-tuning and AI engineer base pay averages $206K in 2026 (https://callsphere.ai/blog/vw9c-ai-voice-engineer-hiring-market-2026-salaries-comp); BCG X now hires Forward Deployed AI Engineers straight from campus at $110-190K, showing the role has gone mainstream beyond Palantir (https://managementconsulted.com/bcg-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/); domain expertise in contact centers is the scarce half of the FDE skill pair.

dossier.key_numbers: FDE median base $190-207K, mid-level TC $180-260K, postings up ~800% (https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer; recruitingfromscratch.com)
dossier.skeptic: Technical interviews screen for real engineering depth, not AI-assisted shipping; equity-heavy at the top. The 1099 implementation-contractor path ($100-200/hr) is the reachable version. Survives.
